title: Runtime adapter: probabilistic alias resolution for hybrid tool/function calls
creator: Aisha Moreno
description:
Problem: Customers use a mix of OpenAI-style tool descriptors and older 'legacy function' payloads. Names, casing, and semantics differ (e.g., 'get_user', 'GetUser', 'user.fetch'), and models sometimes emit partial or fuzzy names when streaming. We need a runtime adapter that resolves these to the correct handler with low latency, preserves structured outputs, and degrades gracefully when ambiguous.

Goal: Implement a probabilistic alias resolution layer that sits in the request pipeline (pre-invocation) to map incoming tool/function identifiers to the best candidate handler, apply confidence thresholds, and support deterministic fallback policies. The layer should be transparent to callers, integrate with existing tool registry APIs, collect metrics for alias collisions, and provide a small backfill utility for historical logs so we can retroactively map legacy invocations to canonical names for analytics and billing consistency.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime resolves >=98% of canonical tool calls in our internal testset (100k simulated invocations) with zero additional median latency >1ms
When confidence < 0.55, runtime follows configured fallback: either (a) try exact-match legacy registry, or (b) return structured ambiguity error with candidate list (configurable per-customer)
Telemetry emitted for all ambiguous resolves with candidate scores, resolved key, and decision path
Integration tests for streaming cases where tool name is emitted over multiple tokens (simulated streaming) pass end-to-end with correct invocation in >=95% of cases
Migration/backfill utility can process 30M historical logs in <6 hours using batch job and produce mapping report
technical_notes:
Design summary:
1) Component sits after parser/intent detection and before tool dispatch. Called 'alias-adapter'.
2) Resolution model: hybrid deterministic + lightweight ML scoring. Steps:
   - exact lookup against canonical registry (fast path)
   - normalization heuristics (case-fold, punctuation, snake->camel, prefix stripping)
   - fuzzy match using trigram distance and token overlap (heuristic score)
   - small learned model (LR on features: trigram_score, token_overlap, length_ratio, historical_count) that outputs confidence in [0,1]
3) Streaming support: keep partial-name buffer keyed by request. If streaming emits name progressively, adapter updates candidate scores incrementally; if confidence crosses 'stream_commit_threshold' (0.75 default), commit call without waiting for full name; else wait for end-of-stream token or threshold of tokens.
4) Fallback policies (configurable per-customer): exact_legacy_lookup -> present_candidates -> error -> test-call-safe-mode (call a no-op wrapper to validate)
5) Signature reconciliation: when name maps to a handler with different parameter schema, use a signature-mapper table to translate keys and types. Implement conservative type coercion rules and emit warning header for downstream consumers.
6) Caching: in-memory LRU for hot aliases with TTL=1h and an optimistic write-through to canonical-registry to record alias->canonical mapping when confidence >=0.95.
7) Backfill tool: Map historical 'call_name' fields via same resolution pipeline (batch mode) with an output CSV of (original_name, canonical_key, confidence, chosen_policy).
8) Observability: emit span attributes: alias_candidates, chosen_key, confidence, fallback_reason. Add Prometheus counters for ambiguous_calls_total and alias_cache_hits.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Using a lightweight LR model keeps inference cost low and deterministic compared to a heavy transformer.
- Configurable thresholds let enterprise customers favor safety (no auto-commit) vs latency (stream-commit).
- Opportunistic optimistic caching speeds common hot paths but requires TTL to handle evolving mappings and rollouts.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag behind 'alias_adapter_v2' per-organization.
2) Canary rollout to 5 internal orgs and 10% of traffic for 48h. Monitor false-invocation rate and invocation latency.
3) If error rate < 0.1% and ambiguous_calls_total trend stable, increase to 50% for 24h.
4) Full rollout with migration window: enable optimistic cache backfill job to populate alias cache prior to final flip.
5) Provide customer opt-out and 'strict_mode' where only exact matches allowed.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for normalization heuristics, scoring features, and signature mapping (target coverage >90%).
- Integration tests: simulate streaming token sequences that form tool names across boundary conditions.
- Load test: 10k rps with 50 token average message size, assert p50 latency delta <1ms and p99 <5ms.
- Regression test: ensure existing 'function calling' e2e tests remain green.
- Security review: ensure no arbitrary code execution path by enforcing handler registry whitelist and rejecting mappings that point to disabled handlers.
